why_this_file_exists: Gate 2 excused foundry_family_sweep by ROW NAME. The row was authorized to carry six standing blocking findings; it carried SEVEN on 2026-08-14 and Gate 2 still printed [KNOWN] and still exited GREEN. A waiver keyed on a row name cannot tell a new failure from the one it forgave, and this is the end-to-end proof.

The identity of a blocking finding is its STRUCTURED semantics, never its prose. `detail` is an English sentence that gets reworded whenever the check's message improves; `(kind, subject)` is what the check actually decided. A waiver keyed on prose would go stale on a typo fix.

ONE source of truth. foundry_family_sweep reads this file and decides; foundry_gate2 reads nothing and only interprets the tool's exit status. Duplicating these six in the runner would recreate the mirror-drift defect the sweep itself was built to catch.

how_it_is_enforced.exit_0: no blocking findings AND no authorized debt -- fully clean
how_it_is_enforced.exit_3: blocking findings exactly equal this authorized set -- KNOWN debt, the only excusable outcome
how_it_is_enforced.exit_1: anything else: an unauthorized blocker, an authorized blocker that vanished (stale waiver / XPASS -- the waiver itself changed and needs review, never a silent celebration), a substitution at the same count, or any infrastructure failure such as a missing codebook

retirement: When a W6 item is genuinely fixed, DELETE its row here in the same commit. The gate will go RED until you do, on purpose -- that is the stale-waiver check, and it is the half that stops this file from outliving the debt.
